# The Exodus of Autumn's First Light

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit." — Psalm 147:4-5

## Reflection
As the fall season begins, the night sky performs its own quiet migration. The Summer Triangle—Vega, Deneb, and Altair—slowly sinks toward the western horizon, while the star Fomalhaut, the "Solitary One of Autumn," rises alone in the southeast. Unlike the clustered brilliance of summer, this season's sky feels sparser, more contemplative. The Milky Way begins its long descent, and the constellations that dominated our warm evenings seem to be leaving us.

But they aren't gone—they're merely moving into a different part of the story. The stars aren't lost when we stop seeing them. They remain faithfully in their courses through the changing seasons.

There may be seasons in your faith that feel like an exodus—when familiar comforts, visible blessings, or spiritual "summer seasons" seem to fade. Yet God's naming of every star reminds us that nothing in creation—and nothing in your life—escapes His intimate attention. The same God who calls Deneb and Fomalhaut by name calls you beloved. He doesn't merely count your days; He knows your name, your struggles, and your place in His grand unfolding story.

## Prayer
Lord of the autumn skies, when my seasons shift and familiar lights fade from view, remind me that You still see me clearly. You who name each star know my name too. Anchor me in the faithful rhythm of Your love, even as my own seasons change. Amen.
